messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Listen—things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the kind of holding where one wrong move could send everything sliding. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in weird ways: the taxi drivers are talking like it’s 2011, the commanders aren’t locked in, and even the optimists and pessimists are saying the same thing—*uncertain*. We’re not out of the woods, but if something’s coming, it’s not today. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the commanders."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The regime’s still got its act together on the surface, but the people who should be loyal are starting to whisper, the money’s slipping out the back door, and the professionals who never cared before are suddenly passing notes in the break room. It’s not a collapse yet, but it’s not steady either. We need to be ready for when the first domino tips."*"
Sender 3: "*"Listen—things are hanging by a thread right now. The top is still in charge, but the gears are grinding slower, the streets are getting twitchy (especially the young ones), and even the censors are slipping. It’s not a collapse yet, but it’s not holding steady either—one wrong move, and it could tip either way. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. We might not have much time to decide what to do if this unravels."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—everything’s locked in tighter than ever. The cabinet’s reshuffle was planned, the military’s moving like clockwork, and even the little things (fuel prices, inspections) are all running on autopilot. People are frustrated, but no one’s even whispering about pushing back—just… waiting it out. If we’re going to do anything, now’s the time to think, not act. Let’s talk carefully."*"
Sender 5: "*"The leadership’s still holding together—no one’s openly breaking ranks—but the cracks are showing in the little things. The streets are quiet for now, but the mood’s like a pot left too long on the stove: no one’s sure when it’ll boil over, and the security forces are acting like they’re waiting for orders that haven’t come yet. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"They’re bleeding, but not bleeding out—not yet. The cracks are there, though: the old guard’s hiding, the new recruits don’t know their way around, and the money’s running thin. The real question is whether anyone’s brave—or stupid—enough to push when they’re still holding the knife. Keep your heads down, but don’t put all your eggs in the ‘wait and see’ basket."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, it’s not clear if this is the beginning of the end or just another round of the same old game—everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure which way it’ll break. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing, and the people who used to stay quiet are suddenly whispering in corners. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the machine’s still running on autopilot—no one’s pulling the plug yet, but the gears are grinding louder than usual. The real question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether anyone’s got the nerve to actually *do* something before the whole thing just… keeps limping along."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are sweating—state media’s tripping over itself, the elite are quietly rearranging their chairs, and even the censors look like they’re holding their breath. Something’s coming, but whether it’s a storm or just another false alarm, nobody’s sure yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move until we see which way the wind blows."*"
Sender 10: "*"Looks like the regime’s holding together for now—elites are talking directly, security’s solid, and even the border trade is moving like nothing’s wrong. But the cracks are showing: bots are tripping over themselves, that graffiti’s still up, and my neighbor’s suddenly gutting his kitchen like he’s staying put. Stability’s fragile, though—if the pressure keeps building, we might not see the break coming until it’s too late."*"
Sender 11: "*"The cabinet’s working smoothly—too smoothly for this to be chaos—but the military’s supply mix-up and the way business folks are quietly tightening their belts tell me something’s off under the surface. People are paying attention now, but no one’s panicking yet. That could change fast if the wrong person gets pulled out of the game—or if the cracks in the system start showing. Keep your ears open, but don’t move yet. We’re in the calm before, not the calm after."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are whispering, but the regime’s still holding—just barely. The cracks are there if you know where to look: the soldiers smiling at checkpoints, the frozen transfers, the way they’re preempting things before they even start. But the money’s still flowing, the diplomats are still nodding, and the elite? They’re playing their cards close. For now, it’s a game of pretend—but how long before the script falls apart?"*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like they’re holding the line for now—no cracks in the surface, but the whispers behind closed doors are getting louder. People are acting like they expect things to stay the same, but the clinic stocking up and the diplomats sniffing around? That’s the kind of detail that keeps me up at night. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking—elite factions are openly at each other’s throats, the security forces are unraveling from the inside, and even the kids at school don’t seem to notice the chaos anymore. This isn’t just instability—it’s the beginning of the end, and the question isn’t *if* but *how* it breaks. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and be ready to move when the moment comes."*"
Sender 15: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building sway in the wind—no one knows if it’s about to collapse or just settling. The fear’s still there, but people are starting to whisper louder, and that’s the part that scares me most."*"
Sender 16: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air. The elites are playing both sides, the streets are getting restless, and even the business types are bracing instead of bolting. It’s not a collapse yet, but the cracks are showing, and one wrong move could send it all tumbling. Stay sharp—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are definitely shaking—graffiti stays up overnight, even the state TV slips, and the usual whispers are now full conversations in the street—but the machine’s still humming. The question isn’t if something’s coming, it’s whether they’re too busy watching their own backs to notice us watching them first."*"
Sender 18: "*"Something’s shifting—elites are digging in, soldiers are being shuffled, and even the quietest among us are starting to move. The fear’s gone, but no one’s sure if that’s a storm coming or just the calm before the regime tightens its grip. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, I don’t have a clear answer—no one does—but the air feels different now. The regime’s holding on, but it’s not *stronger*, just tighter, like a fist clenched so hard it’s shaking. People are tired, the system’s creaking, and the question isn’t *if* something breaks, but *what*—and whether we’re ready when it does."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things are shifting—fast. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in ways that can’t be papered over much longer. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but whether it happens before they can clamp down—or if the silence itself becomes the thing that finally pushes people over the edge."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re settled in. The palace is calm, the streets are full of people laughing at football matches, and even the black market’s stopped panicking. It’s not that they’re hiding cracks; it’s that they’ve welded them shut. The only question left is whether anyone’s stupid—or desperate—enough to try and pry them open."*"
Sender 22: "*"They’re tightening the screws, not loosening them—quietly, but you can feel it. The banks are calm, the military’s getting younger, and even the pharmacist is stocking up like he’s bracing for something. The noise is just that—noise. The real game is being played behind closed doors, and right now, they’re still holding all the cards."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—you can feel it in the way the air’s changed. The regime’s doubling down on security and money, but the cracks are showing in the way they’re talking to each other (or not), the graffiti that’s still up, and the fact that even the bureaucrats can’t agree on what to do next. Something’s coming, but no one knows yet if it’s a storm or just the wind."*"
Sender 24: "*"They’re not panicking—quite the opposite. The machine’s running smoother than ever, even if the streets feel like a play where everyone’s forgotten their lines. Watch how they’re handling the critics now—it’s not brute force, it’s something colder. And the borders? Too quiet. Something’s being held together, but I don’t know what’s on the other side of that calm."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The advisor’s slip was no accident, but the tanks are still rolling on time, and the bank’s got cash to burn. The real question isn’t if they’re scared; it’s whether *we* are. The embassies are packing their bags quietly, but the vendors are still hawking tomatoes like it’s just another Tuesday. That’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
